newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia to announce two new hotels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia to announce two new hotels - paper.

text.p: Philadelphia officials and developers are preparing to announce plans to construct two new hotels in the city, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.

The new construction, part of an effort to attract a Democratic or Republican national convention in 2000, would help alleviate a shortage in hotel rooms that has developed since a new convention center opened in 1993.

The plan closest to an actual groundbreaking is a $20 million, 292-room hotel in a 16-story former garment factory at 1100 Vine Street. The other is a $54 million hotel planned for Two Mellon Center on South Penn Square.
Part of the financing would come from loans from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, channeled through the Philadelphia Industrial Development Corp, the paper reported.
